ingredients.item: whole mackerel , gutted and cleaned, heads on or off , or 4 thick cross-cut steaks
coarse salt — more than seems right; see Method
lemon or a splash of rice vinegar , optional but traditional beside
toasted sesame seeds and sliced scallion , for the platter
Steamed rice , kimchi — the fatty-fish law is a fermented cut beside it — mu sangchae , and a bowl of the soy-vinegar onion dip

instructions.heading: Oiled grate, skin down, over the moderate zone — and leave it alone
instructions.action: Oiled grate, skin down, over the moderate zone — and leave it alone. Whole fish need 5–6 minutes on the first side; steaks 3–4. The skin will stick and then release itself as it crisps — the earliest tongs attempt tears the skin off and the skin is half the dish.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the skin is done when it lifts cleanly and shows crisp gold-brown with darker grill stripes; at the thickest score, the flesh below is opaque halfway to the bone. Fat will drip and flare — move the fish to the cool zone for 20 seconds when it does, back to finish. This dance is the whole technique.

instructions.heading: The one flip, gently
instructions.action: The one flip, gently. Two spatulas or one wide fish spatula and a confident turn: flesh side (or second steak face) down for 4–5 minutes on the moderate zone. The second side takes less time than the first — the fish is half-cooked already.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the doneness read at the backbone, the record's core test: at the thickest score on the second side, the flesh at the bone has just turned opaque and pulls away from the bone with a fork's gentle sideways nudge. Opaque-at-the-bone is done; translucent-at-the-bone is 2 more minutes; falling-apart is past. Mackerel is fatty enough to stay moist a full minute past done — use that grace, do not fear i

instructions.heading: The plate is the filet lesson
instructions.action: The plate is the filet lesson. Whole fish to a warm platter; the top fillet lifts off the bones in one piece with a spatula run along the backbone (peel from head-end to tail). The skeleton lifts clear in one motion, the second fillet lies beneath — the oldest two-fillets-one-fish service in the world. Sesame and scallion over, lemon or vinegar beside.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: eating test: a flake of the thick loin with a strand of kimchi — crisp skin in the same bite, rich sweet fat, the fermented cut answering it. If the flesh tastes under-seasoned, the cure ran shy (fix next fish: the full 2 teaspoons); the vinegar splash at the table is the patch, not the cure.

visualDonenessCues: The fish: cured with the full salt measure, dried uncovered, skin patted bone-dry, thickest part scored to the bone.
The fire: moderate with a cool zone; the skin releases itself — never forced.
The pull: flesh opaque at the backbone at the thickest score, pulling from the bone with a nudge.
The plate: two fillets off one skeleton, skin crisp, fermented cut beside every plate.
storageNotes: The salted fish holds 24 hours refrigerated (the cure is the keeping). Cooked, 2 days — the leftover fillet flaked over rice with sesame oil and a fried egg is the home table's day-after classic, arguably better than the first night.

Variations: hairtail runs the same cure sliced into fingers (#SF08); yellow croaker runs it whole and drier-salted (#SF09); a gochujang swipe in the last 2 minutes takes it toward the yangnyeom lane for the spicy table.
